strings.text: One summer on an island in a pale northern sea: a grandmother who is getting old and a six-year-old girl who lost her mother this spring. Before the summer ends the grandmother can give her one thing — the truth, protection, or the summer itself. What will she give, and what will be left ungiven?
An island for one summer, an old woman and a little girl — and what will Grandmother have time to give her?
after the novel by Tove Jansson

Half a promise: the new house, “at night, some day.”

Grandmother. The moon’s in the water
“I don’t know. She isn’t here any more. That’s for ever”

In heaven. And she sees you

There’s a beetle! A red one!

Let’s go out on the porch. Let’s look at it
It isn’t you. It’s the sky. Look at it
Row, little boat, past the last of the stones… the gull is asleep and the herring… mm-mm… sleeps too… the light on the skerry is… mm… is burning for you

Nothing at all to do with me?

Will you put it up yourself?

There aren’t many other times left for us
Candle for two hours. If the fog comes — don’t move from the spot. Not toward a light, not toward a voice. That’s the law
Mamma, I’ll write to the doctor
“If you get frightened — call. I’ll hear”

I wasn’t frightened! I was asleep!

Mama, I’m alone. Hardly frightened at all
She isn’t getting up! She said — then to you!
I called and you didn’t come!
I was alone! All night! By myself!
“I’ll knock” — broken, though she was behind the canvas.
The winter will carry it off

You’ll winter with us. The doctor will come

Along the shore. So that I can see
She wouldn’t have let herself be led either

This spring Sophia’s mother died. That summer, as always, they lived on the island: Papa, Sophia and Grandmother
Soon. But that is not the least concern of yours

If you keep it, the chapters after this one will have to be played again.
Thunder, and a blanket over two heads.
A full cup, and Papa talking about the doctor.
Wet stones, fog white under the moon, and no lantern.
The second door creaks, and Papa sleeps on the veranda.
Wet stones, white fog, and somewhere the tent.
The gangway rail, and the boat waiting.
The boat waits at the gangway.
A small hand in an old one, and the moon in the window.
A small hand, and the island going into the white.
A piece of driftwood, a knife, and somewhere inside it a seal.
Wet canvas, and a girl talking on the other side of it.
A lamp at the window, and a light going away into the white.
Slippery rock, cold water, and the ledge under it.
The ground swims, and the grey trees go round.
A net pulled into a knot, and two pairs of hands.
Two pairs of hands on the oars, and a hundred strokes to the boat.
Sophia leans on the oars under the old hands.
Two beds side by side, and a gap of a blanket between them.
A parcel with a label, and Sophia pulling it her way.
Sophia pulls, and the string goes taut.
She sits down on a low stone to get her breath.
The sea like glass, and a pebble in an old hand.
Not a ripple on the glass. Nothing moves.
The peonies are thick, and somewhere under them are her teeth.
A pole on bare rock, and a girl tying knots.
Two old hands on the gunwale, and the boat wants to go.
The boat stirs under the hands: the sea is pulling it.
Rain, white sky, and the porch rail wet under the hands.
Under the clear water a ledge, and the girl’s shoulder under an old hand.
The shoulder stirs under the hand: the ledge is so near.
Small fingers clutching an old sleeve.
The small fingers loosen on the sleeve.
A candle, and a small palm on an old breast.
Stones in the dark, and a lantern in an old hand.
A rocking boat, and the fog closing behind.
A lamp in the window, and the cape white with fog.
Sophia leans out over the water, and the ledge goes down into the dark.
Grandmother spent her strength on the summer
Grandmother’s strength: how much of her body is left for this summer. Kept herself — or spent it on the summer: the more she spends, the further the bar goes.
Sophia: hand in hand — on her own. Whether the girl holds on to Grandmother or goes by herself.
Sophia will remember: Grandmother held her by the wrist.
Sophia will remember: Grandmother let her go.
Papa saw his mother climb out of the water.
A secret for two: Grandmother smokes.
No secret any more: a shell on the veranda rail.
The packet is deep in the crevice: Grandmother has given up.
Papa will remember: the net untangled together, and his question left unanswered.
Sophia stroked the cat for the first time.
From now on Sophia buries everything dead she finds.
The cat is put out for the night now.
Sophia was told the truth: Mama is not here any more.
Papa knows about her head. Now he decides.
Sophia knows about her head — and promised not to tell Papa.
Sophia will remember: they looked at the storm together.
Sophia will remember: the song under the blanket.
Sophia will remember: it was not her doing.
Sophia will remember: being afraid is allowed.
Grandmother promised: “At midnight I’ll knock. Three times.”
